{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I designed the entire user interface for our startup's app—every screen, every interaction. When we won a design award, my CEO accepted it saying 'I've always believed good design starts at the top.' He framed the award in his office. I still have my original sketches in a drawer.

CANDIDATE A:
In high school, I choreographed our dance team's competition routine. Our coach submitted it to a choreography competition under her own name and won regional recognition. She used the certificate to negotiate a raise. I learned about it from a newspaper clipping.

CANDIDATE B:
I designed a new product feature over six months. When it increased user engagement, my supervisor credited me by name in the all-hands meeting. The CEO mentioned my contribution in the quarterly report.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:24"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve an individual who contributed significantly to a project but was overshadowed by someone in a higher position who took credit for the success."}
